title: TS SDK: runtime-safe union builders with Zod + JSON-Schema emit and streaming shape hints
creator: Daniel Park
description: Problem: consumers using the TypeScript SDK need a reliable way to declare structured output contracts (discriminated unions) that are usable at both compile-time and runtime, work well with streaming partial results, and can be validated with either Zod or downstream JSON-Schema validators. This ticket implements: 1) a generator that emits lightweight runtime factories for discriminated unions, 2) optional Zod wrappers for ergonomic runtime validation and inference, 3) JSON-Schema emit for customers integrating with external validators (AJV, browser runtimes), and 4) streaming 'shape hints' used by the streaming parser to validate partial chunks and provide early errors. Goals: - Preserve full type safety for callers using generated types. - Keep runtime overhead minimal for hosted use. - Provide migration helpers for existing customers using manual validators. - Add examples and tests covering sync/async parsing, streaming incremental validation, and function-calling shaped outputs.
acceptance_criteria: CLI generator emits TypeScript types + runtime factory functions for discriminated unions
Generated factories have a Zod-based optional wrapper that can be imported as
JSON-Schema emit option generates draft-07 compatible schemas for each union variant
Streaming parser accepts shape-hints and can validate partial tokens without waiting for full object
Docs and code examples added to tsdk/examples/structured-output with Node/browser examples
Unit + integration tests for generator, runtime factories, streaming validator, and migration guide
No change to existing public SDK surface unless opt-in via new generator flag
design_notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Keep the runtime factories minimal (handrolled checks) vs full Zod-only approach. Chosen approach: emit tiny hand-rolled runtime predicates for hot paths and provide optional Zod validators for heavy-duty checks. 2) JSON-Schema generation will be a deterministic mapping from the type AST; we will not try to preserve Zod-specific refinements (documented). 3) Streaming validation uses 'shape hints' which are lightweight partial schemas (required keys + discriminant) to validate early; full validation is performed once the object completes. Performance expectations: on microbenchmarks, hand-rolled predicates must be ~2-4x faster than Zod for simple unions. Security: emitted factories must not eval() arbitrary strings. Code generation will be string-safe and TypeScript-only.
implementation_plan: spec: define AST -> types/runtime/zod/jsonschema mapping (3 days)
generator: implement emitters and CLI flags (4 days)
runtime: implement streaming shape-hint consumer and incremental validator (3 days)
tests: unit & integration test matrix across Node/browser (2 days)
docs: examples, migration guide, and performance notes (2 days)
review: engineering + DX review + release cut (1 day)
